entry.title: Paleokastritsa Beach
entry.summary: A cluster of small coves on the north-west coast of Corfu, backed by green hills and cliffs. Agios Spyridon is the main beach, and boats from the harbour run to sea caves and quieter coves.

entry.title: Plakias Beach
entry.summary: A long sandy beach of about 1.3 km on the south coast of Crete, roughly 40 km from Rethymno. The village behind has tavernas, shops and supermarkets, and quieter stretches lie under the trees.

entry.title: Playa de Calahonda
entry.summary: A small cove in the old town of Nerja, reached through a little arch behind the Balcon de Europa and a zigzag of steps down to the sand. Cliffs frame the beach and the cafes of the town centre are a short walk above.

entry.title: Praia do Barril
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach on the barrier island of the Ria Formosa, reached from Santa Luzia by a flat footpath or a short tourist train. Rows of rusting anchors in the dunes behind the sand are a memorial to the local tuna fishing community.

entry.title: Is Arutas
entry.summary: A beach on the Sinis peninsula in west Sardinia, known for sand made of tiny quartz grains in many colours that give the shallow water a clear, bright look. It is one of the best-known beaches of the Oristano coast.

entry.title: Arromanches Gold Beach
entry.summary: A broad sandy beach below chalk cliffs, known as Gold Beach in the 1944 landings. At low tide the concrete remains of the Mulberry harbour appear offshore, and the small town behind has museums, cafes and a seafront promenade.

entry.title: Praia do Castelejo
entry.summary: A wide Atlantic beach on the wild western Algarve, set below tilted dark schist cliffs and rolling hills. Waves are strong, the water is cold and the beach stays quiet even in summer, with surfers and walkers as the main visitors.

entry.title: Playa de la Barrosa
entry.summary: An 8 km sweep of fine golden sand on the Costa de la Luz, backed by pine woods and a low red cliff at the north end. At low tide the sand flats and rock pools stretch far out, and the sunsets over the Atlantic are the main event.

entry.title: Praia de Burgau
entry.summary: A small sandy beach in the western Algarve, backed by the whitewashed houses of Burgau village and framed by green hills. Swimming is usually calmer than on the open west coast.

entry.title: El Cotillo Beach
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach near the fishing village of El Cotillo on the north-west coast of Fuerteventura, known for clear turquoise water, steady wind and windsurfers.

entry.title: Playa de las Canteras
entry.summary: A long, sheltered city beach in Las Palmas, protected by a natural offshore reef that keeps the water calm for most of the year. A promenade runs the whole length.

entry.title: Maspalomas Dunes
entry.summary: A protected field of golden dunes at the southern tip of Gran Canaria, running down to a wide Atlantic beach. Walking through the dunes takes effort but the views are worth it.

entry.title: Playa de Zahara de los Atunes
entry.summary: A long, wide beach of fine pale sand on Spain's Atlantic coast, with big skies and strong evening light. Wind and surf can be strong on this stretch.

entry.title: Playa de Cabopino
entry.summary: A sandy beach on the Costa del Sol beside the small Cabopino marina and an old watchtower, backed by pine woods and dunes. Part of the beach is used by naturists.

entry.title: Ilha de Tavira
entry.summary: A long barrier island off the eastern Algarve with wide sandy beaches, calm lagoon water on one side and the open Atlantic on the other. Reached by a short ferry or boat from Tavira.

entry.title: Praia do Seixal
entry.summary: A small beach of dark volcanic sand on the north coast of Madeira, framed by steep green cliffs. A natural sea pool and a few cafes sit nearby.

entry.title: Praia do Meco
entry.summary: A long, open Atlantic beach on the coast south of Lisbon, backed by low cliffs, with golden sand, strong surf and a relaxed local feel.

entry.title: Praia de Alvor
entry.summary: A long, wide sandy beach next to the Alvor estuary in the western Algarve, with space to spread out and calm conditions on most summer days.

entry.title: Playa de Sotavento
entry.summary: A very long beach of pale sand on the south of Fuerteventura, with a shallow turquoise lagoon and a sandbar that changes with the tides. Wide, open and often windy.

entry.title: Praia da Albandeira
entry.summary: A small, sheltered cove at the foot of golden limestone cliffs in the Algarve, with a natural rock arch and clear water. Reached by a short path and steps from the clifftop.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Piscinas
entry.summary: A wild, long beach backed by some of the tallest sand dunes in Europe, on the Costa Verde of south-west Sardinia. Open, quiet and a long way from the resort strips.

entry.title: Lama Monachile
entry.summary: A small pebble cove at the foot of Polignano a Mare, framed by tall limestone cliffs and houses built right at the edge. Clear, deep water close to shore and a short walk from the old town.

entry.title: Xigia Beach
entry.summary: A small sandy and rocky cove on the north-east coast of Zakynthos, known for its sulphur springs, cloudy-turquoise water and pale cliffs. Popular with boat trips as well as visitors by road.

entry.title: Triopetra Beach
entry.summary: A long, quiet beach of sand and fine pebbles on the south coast of Crete, named for the three rock formations standing in the water. Calmer and less visited than the big north-coast resorts.

entry.title: Plage de la Gravette
entry.summary: A small sandy beach right beside the old town and port of Antibes, with calm shallow water and a walk to the ramparts.

entry.title: Praia de Santa Cruz
entry.summary: A wide Atlantic beach of golden sand with dramatic rock stacks, popular with surfers and known for its golden evening light.

entry.title: Formentor Beach
entry.summary: A sheltered bay of pale sand and shallow turquoise water at the foot of the Formentor peninsula in northern Mallorca, backed by pine trees.

entry.title: Nugal Beach
entry.summary: A small, secluded pebble cove with clear turquoise water below limestone cliffs and pines, reached on foot along a path from the Makarska coast.

entry.title: Lone Bay
entry.summary: A pebble and rock bay with clear water, shaded by pines in the Zlatni Rt forest park just south of Rovinj, with paths along the coast.

entry.title: Mingardo Beach
entry.summary: A quiet cove of small pebbles and clear water on the Cilento coast, set between green cliffs near Marina di Camerota.
